description: Stable exercise validation codes, in phase order SCHEMA, LINT, COMMAND, SELF_EVALUATION. A finding is {code, path?}; findings never echo content. A lint whose prerequisite already failed is skipped (stated in its rule).

phases.LINT: Semantic lint per mechanic (architecture section 6 table) and reference resolution
phases.COMMAND: The same parse the publication endpoint uses
phases.SELF_EVALUATION: Probes through the same AttemptEvaluation as /exercise-previews

codes.rule: The output violates output.schema.json (exact field sets, bounds, enums, ID patterns). All schema violations of one exercise are one finding with the failing JSON paths.
Every material handle (m1, m1:b3) must exist in the pinned materials of the session.
An objective handle (t1) must be one of the objectives offered in the task.
Local IDs are unique within one exercise (options, blanks, items, categories, left and right items).

The exercise's mechanic must be one of the mechanics the task allows (the session's settings.mechanics; AUTO allows all seven). The context of a fixture may carry allowedMechanics; without it all seven are allowed.
The reference must have nonblank content.
The reference must not equal the prompt after normalization (NFC, trim, case fold, collapsed whitespace).
No accepted answer may occur in the prompt text as whole words after normalization.
Accepted alternatives are distinct after the exercise's own matching rule (normalization, or soft normalization in SOFT mode).
In SOFT mode no alternative may normalize to the empty string.
The key's blank IDs are exactly the blank IDs of the passage, each once.
The passage with accepted[0] filled into every blank must be a fragment (whitespace-normalized) of one block of the pinned material. Evaluated only when the key covers the blanks.
All alternatives of an ANSWER_LENGTH blank have the same length in code points (NFC).
Option texts are distinct after normalization.
SINGLE has exactly one correct option; MULTIPLE has at least one.
No option of the form 'all of the above' or 'none of the above' (per output language) unless the task explicitly asks for it.
pairs is a bijection between left and right: every item once on each side.
Left labels are distinct and right labels are distinct after normalization.
A paired label must not contain the other label of its pair (the pair would be given away).
At least two distinguishable tiles; identical tiles are interchangeable and fewer than two distinct make every arrangement correct.
Every item names an existing category.
At least two categories contain an item.

The compiled command was rejected by ExerciseCommand.readCreate, the parser of the publication endpoint, for a reason the lints above did not catch. A compiler or lint gap; never shown to the model as a rule.
The KEY probe did not evaluate to CORRECT through AttemptEvaluation.
A DISTRACTOR or shifted-pair probe did not evaluate to INCORRECT (or PARTIAL where a fixture says so).
